import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sendov's conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture)

Tags: Sendov Conjecture, Ilieff's Conjecture.

-/

open Polynomial

namespace Sendov

open Sendov

/-- The predicate that a polynomial satisfies the hypotheses of Sendov's conjecture.

`f.IsSendov` holds if `f` has degree at least 2 and all roots of `f` lie in the unit disc
of the complex plane. -/
def Polynomial.IsSendov (f : ℂ[X]) : Prop :=
  2 ≤ f.natDegree ∧ (f.rootSet ℂ ⊆ Metric.closedBall 0 1)

/-- `SatisfiesSendovConjecture n` states that Sendov's conjecture is true for every polynomial of
degree `n`. -/
def Nat.SatisfiesSendovConjecture (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.IsSendov → f.natDegree = n →
    ∀ z, z ∈ f.rootSet ℂ → Metric.infDist z (f.derivative.rootSet ℂ) ≤ 1

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point. -/
@[category research open, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds when the degree of $n$ is at most $9$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine (n : ℕ) (hn : n ∈ Set.Icc 2 9) :
    n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

/-- **Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds for polynomials of sufficiently large degree.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12 30 52]
theorem sendov_conjecture.variants.eventually_true :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture := by
  sorry

end Sendov

findings.description: The hypothesis `n ∈ Set.Icc 2 9` includes degree 9, whereas the cited low-degree result covers only degrees 2 through 8. There is no indexing shift: `SatisfiesSendovConjecture n` explicitly requires `f.natDegree = n`. Thus this variant adds a degree case to the source's bound. The subsequent full solution makes the degree-9 assertion true too, but does not change the bound of the cited historical low-degree result.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia states: “The conjecture was previously proven for n < 9 by Brown and Xiang,” and cites their paper entitled “Proof of the Sendov conjecture for polynomials of degree at most eight” (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture). Tao's arXiv:2012.04125v2, §1, likewise says “specifically for all n < 9”; his 12 August 2026 exposition explicitly identifies the previous bound as n ≤ 8.
findings.suggested_fix: For the cited low-degree result, use `hn : n ∈ Set.Icc 2 8` (equivalently, `Set.Ico 2 9`) and update the variant's name and docstring to say “at most eight.” Alternatively, retain degree 9 only as an explicitly described corollary of the newly cited 2026 full solution.

status_issues.source_status: The source now records the full conjecture as solved. Wikipedia reports a proof posted by Lech Mazur on 5 August 2026 using GPT-5.6 Pro, followed by Tao's verification and exposition on 12 August 2026. Tao explicitly reports resolution for all n ≥ 2 and a Lean verification.
status_issues.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendov%27s_conjecture records the August 2026 resolution. In https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/08/12/a-digestion-of-the-proof-of-sendovs-conjecture/, Tao writes that Mazur was able “to resolve Sendov’s conjecture for all n ≥ 2” and that the argument “resolves both the Sendov conjecture and the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture in full generality.”
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to `research solved` and cite the 2026 resolution. The mathematical statement itself should remain unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Uses `Metric.infDist z (f.derivative.rootSet ℂ) ≤ 1` instead of explicitly asserting the existence of a critical point within distance 1; root sets also discard multiplicities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The hypothesis gives `f.natDegree ≥ 2`. Over ℂ, the derivative has degree `f.natDegree - 1 ≥ 1`, so the fundamental theorem of algebra makes its root set nonempty. This set is finite and hence compact, so the infimum distance is attained. Therefore the inequality is equivalent to `∃ w ∈ f.derivative.rootSet ℂ, dist z w ≤ 1`. Multiplicities do not affect these universal and existential assertions about root locations. The explicit-witness equivalence was proved in the scratch file without using the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: Quantifies over arbitrary complex polynomials satisfying the root and degree hypotheses, rather than requiring the monic normalization used in Wikipedia's product formula.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The degree hypothesis excludes the zero polynomial, so its leading coefficient is nonzero. Multiplication by the inverse leading coefficient makes the polynomial monic while preserving degree, roots, and derivative roots. Consequently, the arbitrary-polynomial and monic-polynomial formulations are equivalent. The fixed-degree equivalence was proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Expresses sufficiently large degree using `∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop` rather than an explicit threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For ℕ, this is equivalent to `∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture`. The threshold precedes the quantification over polynomials and roots, exactly as in Tao's uniform theorem. It can also be increased to ensure `2 ≤ N`. This equivalence was proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04125 — Terence Tao, Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials, v2
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2012.04125 — downloaded LaTeX; abstract, §1 conjecture and main theorem, remarks, and Brown–Xiang bibliography entry
review.notes: Checked both definitions and all three theorem statements. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles successfully; the equivalence proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. Boundary checks exclude zero, constant, and linear polynomials, establish nonvacuous hypotheses using X^n for every n ≥ 2, and verify that X² − 1 attains critical-point distance exactly 1. The reviewed file matches the specified commit, and no repository files were edited.

submission.summary: Changed the low-degree range to `Set.Icc 2 8`, renamed the variant to `Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_eight`, and updated its docstring. All other declarations and attributes were left unchanged. The requested compile command succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
